# Original simple and Phantom object senders

Independent inputs were frozen before original execution or any native change:
3,443 contexts (699 Phantom, 2,744 simple), 3,455 calls and four separate faults.
Both original FPU profiles execute all 183 Phantom +177 simple +17 converter
+61 health-child bytes, 438 total. Every valid context differs between the
profiles. Full original heap/neighbors, outer stack, nonvolatile registers,
control word/TOP and code are guarded. Raw caller-argument scratch and health
partial-register upper words remain diagnostic data in the reference.

The consumer checks actual C and public Go entries against startup execution,
with the actual native converter and C health builder/important queue. The
nearest-profile consumer explicitly replays observed converter results while
checking root load/callback order, state, bytes, flags and complete return word;
it does not claim native alternate-FPU converter support. UnitCode, direction
and publication are declared services. The health network service's unused
return word is a declared input trace value; actual C builder and real queue
packet/recipient are checked, without claiming that network body's equivalence.

C/Go faults retain completed effects. Whole guarded native Object, two generator
update records and two health records are compared, including every untouched
byte. No native store-count, raw x87 state or CGo stack-slot equivalence is claimed.
The old public signatures accepted an Object pointer in a32bitint argument:
valid native Go/C getter controls pass above4GiB, then both actual old C entries
reproduce SIGSEGV. Exact control/crash logs, inputs, producer and outputs remain
under ROOT/simple-phantom-senders-native-entry-port. No original assets are
copied into the repository; fixtures contain observed semantic results only.
